claims.text: The proposed model combines ab initio DFT+CPA simulations with Bayesian machine learning.
The model will predict bulk HfNbTaTiZr conductivity within ±10% of experiment across 0–200 K and 300–1200 K.
CPA can provide a first-principles configurationally averaged description of alloy disorder.
Direct treatment of disorder will make the hybrid model more accurate than perfect-crystal analytical approaches.
Bulk HfNbTaTiZr is considered in a disordered random-solid-solution phase.
The relevant specimens contain processing-induced vacancies or interstitials and may contain 1 wt.% oxygen.
DFT+CPA can compute electronic structure and defect-induced scattering parameters for ensembles containing vacancies, interstitials, and oxygen substitutions.
Bayesian machine learning can calibrate conductivity-scattering parameters from temperature-resolved measurements.
The model is to be calibrated and validated in both the 0–200 K and 300–1200 K regimes for defect-free and 1 wt.% oxygen specimens.
Oxygen-induced distortions, vacancies, and interstitials modify the alloy's electronic band structure and scattering behavior.
Defect states and oxygen substitutions broaden electronic bands and introduce localized electronic states.
The defect-induced electronic changes alter carrier-scattering rates.
Low-temperature conductivity is governed in part by impurity-mediated conduction, whereas high-temperature conductivity exhibits enhanced phonon–defect scattering.
The model predicts a modest increase in impurity-mediated conduction over 0–200 K.
The model predicts enhanced phonon–defect scattering effects over 300–1200 K.
A greater-than-±10% discrepancy between predicted and measured conductivity at 350 K for the 1 wt.% oxygen specimen will falsify the hypothesis.
Conventional analytical conductivity predictions generally assume perfect, defect-free crystals and neglect processing defects and oxygen impurities.
The proposed applicability range is bulk HfNbTaTiZr with typical defect densities and no more than 1 wt.% oxygen.
Predictions for extreme doping or grain-boundary-dominated engineered microstructures may require model extensions.
Single-site CPA may not capture local defect clustering.
